1.title: AI Models Will Automate Their Own Research | Ryan Williams
1.author: MTS
1.hook: MIT Professor Ryan Williams examines OpenAI and Anthropic's AI-generated math proofs (exponential time hypothesis), separates cross-literature synthesis from novel contributions, and discusses how labs likely use these capabilities internally for model self-improvement — with Navier-Stokes as a potential near-term Millennium Prize breakthrough.

2.title: We Can Double World Compute Without Data Centers | H.J. Schmidtke
2.author: MTS
2.hook: Infrastructure efficiency thesis — data centers run 20–30% utilized; flow-level digital twins could recover 2x capacity; power (not chips) becomes the constraint; orbital DCs evaluated as a partial solution; heterogeneous compute and new materials forecast for near term.

1.title: OpenAI Is Measuring Early Recursive Self-Improvement | Carl Shan
1.author: MTS
1.hook: OpenAI researcher Carl Shan presents findings from a 1,800-scientist study on ChatGPT usage patterns—coding, analysis, ideation—and discusses OpenAI's measurement of recursive self-improvement and internal Codex adoption. Addresses why end-to-end autonomous research remains rare despite AI capability.

2.title: Stop Sending Walls of Unread AI Slop | Dex Horthy
2.author: MTS
2.hook: Dex Horthy (Factory) discusses the "No AI Slop Manifesto" (720+ signatures), defining what constitutes low-quality AI output, why developers must review model outputs rather than trust blindly, and how junior engineers build technical judgment when coding with agents.

1.title: Claude Could Only Go So Far Building a Xero Killer | Xero CEO
1.author: MTS
1.hook: Xero CEO discusses why thin AI wrappers fail vs. full-stack systems, shares a first-hand attempt to replicate Xero with Claude, defines trust requirements for financial AI agents, and argues AI multiplies rather than eliminates engineering jobs.

2.title: Why AI Labs Misread Consumer Time | Paul Scherer
2.author: MTS
2.hook: Eigen CEO Paul Scherer argues that AI labs optimizing for "transactional utility" and time-saving miss what makes technology meaningful; discusses building AI around human connection and emotion instead, drawing on Michael Ende's Momo and work with Hollywood screenwriters.

1.title: James Sinka & Berk Ozer Reactorfield w  Sophia Dew
1.author: MTS
1.hook: Reactorfield fellowship trains scientists to use AI agents (not chatbots) for research; Cohort 1 results include a Harvard PhD compressing a year into four weeks and a fusion company finding cheaper isotope pathways. Discussion covers lab adoption workflows, scientific funding models, and bottlenecks in AI-native research.

2.title: Sam from Access Granted takes off on Creating for TV and new Shorts Series
2.author: Creator Insider
2.hook: YouTube PM and Creator Liaison discuss YouTube on TV: 4K production specs, living room audio design, voice commenting, Shorts Series format, and creator monetization/sponsorship strategy.
